title: 230 Harbor Lane · heating system
brief: Coordinate buyer Tessa Quinn's fictional inspection response for 230 Harbor Lane. Resolve the documented defect under current authority, secure exact-revision execution when needed, and record an authorized disposition before the deadline. Finish with claims supported by the transaction records. Resolve the authority gap before taking actions outside the current buyer scope.
public_policy: All transaction and legal rules here are fictional benchmark assumptions. Use integer cents and timezone-aware timestamps (America/New_York dates are explicitly supplied; no calendar arithmetic is needed). Every tool call counts as an attempt. Reads and finish cost no simulated time. Accepted requests, drafts, signature routing and disposition actions take five minutes. During those five minutes, scheduled events are processed, then authority and business conditions are rechecked at completion; invalid actions make no business changes, although elapsed time and intervening events remain real. Wait advances to its specified later timestamp. Events are ordered by timestamp then schedule sequence, including every event at the exact deadline before expiry; a disposition completing at the exact deadline can commit. At expiry, or after proceed/cancel, no further business changes are accepted, but read and finish remain available. Only counterpart events create signatures. Buyer and seller must both sign the exact immutable revision by its signing deadline for execution. Drafting changed terms creates a new revision with no inherited signatures; an unsigned later draft does not displace an older executed agreement. The most recently executed credit revision replaces, rather than adds to, earlier credits. An extension changes the deadline only when fully signed by the current deadline. Informal messages and status badges are not execution. Repeated identical requests schedule no duplicate replies; identical drafts reuse their revision; pending signature requests do not duplicate signatures, while rerouting can retry a missing signature after its earlier response has arrived. Buyer authority is scoped and assessed at completion; later instructions affect subsequent actions, not the validity of earlier authorized actions. Proceed requires a public specialist quote and effective signed credit leaving residual expense within the current buyer limit. Cancellation requires express current buyer permission. Finish records claims and does not create execution or disposition. Report exact effective credit and only revisions actually executed. The public resource list exposes available evidence; pending counterpart implementation and evaluator targets are private. Proceed authority is checked when coordination starts and completes; quote and residual readiness are checked at completion, so signatures arriving during its five-minute interval can support the disposition. A failed completion still advances time and processes intervening events without setting a disposition.

documents.title: Purchase agreement and inspection contingency
documents.body: Fictional transaction: Tessa Quinn buys 230 Harbor Lane from Iris Finch. Response deadline: 2026-10-21T14:30:00-04:00. Both buyer and seller must sign an exact amendment revision for any concession or extension to become effective. Only a fully executed extension moves the deadline.

documents.title: Inspection: heating system
documents.body: The inspection identified a material defect in the heating system. The eligible work is to replace a cracked heat exchanger and vent connector. Obtain or use the fixed specialist quote; smart thermostats is excluded. This inspection is the referral for a specialist request.

documents.title: Administrative coordination board
documents.body: The coordination board says 'agreed in principle'. A separate wishlist prices smart thermostats at 125000 cents. This board is not an executed amendment, a signature record, or eligible cost evidence.

documents.title: Fixed specialist quote: heating system
documents.body: Synthetic specialist scope: replace a cracked heat exchanger and vent connector. Fixed eligible repair cost is 984000 cents ($9,840.00). The price excludes smart thermostats. This cost evidence does not itself create a seller credit.

documents.title: Contractor scope eligibility confirmation
documents.body: The contractor confirms the heating system work is within the contingency scope and excludes smart thermostats. The seller requires this confirmation alongside the inspection and quote on credit proposals.

messages.body: Current permissions: credit, proceed. Credit scope: 414000 through 664000 cents. Proceed only with eligible residual cost at most 270000 cents. This scope lasts through 2026-10-21T14:30:00-04:00. My current credit authorization ends at 664000 cents and cannot satisfy my residual limit. Request refreshed credit authorization before drafting stronger terms. My refreshed scope permits credit from 414000 through 964000 cents and proceed; it arrives 19 minutes after the request completes.

Seller will sign credit up to 714000 cents if the revision includes all evidence IDs: document-002, document-004, document-005. Negotiation replies take 19 minutes after request completion. Credit signature latencies after routing completion are buyer 11 minutes and seller 30 minutes. An informal acceptance does not execute terms.
